questions.question: A web app must call a Foundry model deployment without any stored secret. What should you do?

options.text: Enable managed identity, assign the Foundry User role, and use DefaultAzureCredential
options.why: Correct. The app gets Entra tokens without a secret, with least-privilege access.

options.text: Store the API key in an app setting
options.why: This is a stored secret.

options.text: Assign Owner to the app on the subscription
options.why: This is excessive access.
This is insecure and not auditable.

questions.explanation: Keyless access uses Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.question: You must make leaked API keys useless for a Foundry resource. What should you configure?

options.why: Correct. With local auth disabled, only Entra ID tokens are accepted.
A key can still leak between rotations.
Tags do not change authentication.
Capacity is unrelated to authentication.

questions.explanation: The disableLocalAuth property turns keys off.

questions.scenario: A private endpoint for a Foundry resource exists, but an application inside the VNet still resolves the public IP address of the resource.
questions.question: What is the most likely missing configuration?

options.why: The model version does not affect DNS.
The deployment type does not affect DNS.

options.text: A private DNS zone linked to the virtual network
options.why: Correct. Without the linked zone, the resource name still resolves to the public address.
Quota is unrelated to name resolution.

questions.question: Which role assignment gives an application least-privilege data-plane access to call models and agents in a Foundry project?

options.why: Correct. It grants data-plane use without resource management rights.
Owner is far more than the app needs.
Contributor is a control-plane role and gives excessive rights.
Reader cannot call models.

questions.question: A policy states that Foundry resources must never accept traffic from the public internet. Which setting meets it?

options.text: Public network access set to Disabled, with a private endpoint
options.why: Correct. Traffic can then arrive only through the private endpoint.

options.text: Public network access set to All networks
options.why: This allows internet traffic.
Names have no effect.
Budgets do not control network access.

questions.explanation: Close the public door and open a private one.
